idiom_name: DAO class (or module of async functions) over an injected node-postgres Pool
implementation_notes: In JavaScript the DAO collapses to a small class or module: take a pg.Pool by injection, run parameterised statements with pool.query(text, values) and return plain row objects, because the driver already hands back plain objects and consumers duck-type the implementation. What replaces the classic structure is the language plus dependency injection: no interface declaration is needed, a second store is another object with the same methods, and pool.query is documented as the shortcut that acquires and releases a client internally. Keep the class when a second store is genuinely expected; otherwise one module of async functions per aggregate is the idiomatic minimum.
pitfalls: Inside a transaction you must check out a client with pool.connect() and release it in a finally block; pool.query dispatches each statement to whichever idle client it finds, which the node-postgres documentation warns breaks multi-statement transactions.
A forgotten client.release() exhausts the pool and later calls hang or time out - the pool's waiting queue is the only symptom.
Rows are untyped and column names mirror the database, so map to your own shape at the DAO boundary; otherwise a schema rename ripples through every caller.
